title: Blakey's lessons and giving back; goodbye
summary: Jackson wants to help musicians as Blakey, Elvin and others helped him, recalls Blakey's advice never to put another musician down, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Do you have any last Blakeyisms you want to share with us?
Well I tell you what, I feel that in Art’s honor I want to try to help as many people as I can because I know that’s what he was doing. He wanted to help musicians and I know

that one thing he always told me is don’t put another musician down because if you put another musician down you’re putting yourself down. So I try to, obviously in my recesses we make more judgments about people than we probably should, but I always feel that I should start off with something positive to say about any artist or any musician. Find something positive. Because there really is something there that’s positive. We just choose to look at the negative aspect of it, but everyone doing something has some redeeming quality that we can find, and so I just want to be as helpful to other musicians as Art Blakey was to me, as Elvin was to me, as Freddie Hubbard was to me, Eddie Harris, Stanley Turrentine, all these guys were very available, and Sonny Rollins is available to me, Ron Carter. All these musicians, it’s one big happy community. So I have to be willing to support other people in their endeavors in the way I was supported, and so that would be my Art Blakey — Art Blakey used to wear a tee shirt that said “Experience Teaches” and so I think if I can maybe give some advice and help someone to facilitate their career a little bit, quicker than I did, then that’s my responsibility.
All right. Well said. On that note, I’ll get you to your next engagement. And thanks for your time.
